bibleSpine.kjv: And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
bibleSpine.gloss: The master text: dust (body) + the breath of life (God's life-power) = a living soul. Man does not receive a soul; man BECOMES one. The soul is the sum, not an occupant.

bibleSpine.kjv: In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.
bibleSpine.gloss: God's own verdict on man's constitution and end: dust thou art. What was formed of dust returns to dust — the created being is dissolved, not merely relocated.

bibleSpine.kjv: And the serpent said unto the woman, Ye shall not surely die:
bibleSpine.gloss: The counter-doctrine at its root. The first lie denies Genesis 2:7's mortality: it teaches an undying part in man that death cannot touch. The immortal-soul theory is the serpent's sermon.

bibleSpine.kjv: All in whose nostrils was the breath of life, of all that was in the dry land, died.
bibleSpine.gloss: The same breath of life (Gen. 2:7) is in beast and man alike; when it departs, they die. The breath is life-power common to all creatures, not a distinct conscious human essence.

bibleSpine.kjv: The Spirit of God hath made me, and the breath of the Almighty hath given me life.
bibleSpine.gloss: Defines the breath/spirit: it is the Almighty's own life-giving power, the same act as creation, not a self-conscious tenant lodged in the body.

bibleSpine.kjv: All the while my breath is in me, and the spirit of God is in my nostrils;
bibleSpine.gloss: Job equates 'my breath' with 'the spirit of God in my nostrils' — the spirit that animates man is the breath God breathed (Gen. 2:7), borrowed life-power, not man's own immortal core.

bibleSpine.kjv: If he set his heart upon man, if he gather unto himself his spirit and his breath; All flesh shall perish together, and man shall turn again unto dust.
bibleSpine.gloss: Reverse Genesis 2:7: God gathers back His spirit and breath, and the whole man perishes and returns to dust. Withdraw the life-power and nothing conscious remains.

bibleSpine.kjv: But man dieth, and wasteth away: yea, man giveth up the ghost, and where is he?... So man lieth down, and riseth not: till the heavens be no more, they shall not awake, nor be raised out of their sleep.
bibleSpine.gloss: Death is a sleep from which man does not stir until the resurrection — no conscious survival, only unconscious rest awaiting the trumpet.

bibleSpine.kjv: Thou hidest thy face, they are troubled: thou takest away their breath, they die, and return to their dust.
bibleSpine.gloss: Take away the breath (the life-power) and the creature dies and returns to dust — the exact inverse of Genesis 2:7. Life is a loan sustained moment by moment.

bibleSpine.kjv: Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.
bibleSpine.gloss: Death un-does creation into its two components: dust to earth, spirit (the breath God 'gave') back to God. The spirit returns as impersonal life-power to its Source — it is not the man going to heaven.

bibleSpine.kjv: His breath goeth forth, he returneth to his earth; in that very day his thoughts perish.
bibleSpine.gloss: The instant the breath departs, thoughts PERISH. Consciousness ends with the breath; the mind does not float free. Decisive against a thinking soul surviving death.

bibleSpine.kjv: For the living know that they shall die: but the dead know not any thing, neither have they any more a reward; for the memory of them is forgotten.
bibleSpine.gloss: The dead know nothing — no awareness, no reward yet. The undivided man is simply not conscious in death.

bibleSpine.kjv: For in death there is no remembrance of thee: in the grave who shall give thee thanks?
bibleSpine.gloss: In death there is no remembrance, no praise — no conscious activity of any kind. Corroborates Eccl. 9:5 that the whole man sleeps.

bibleSpine.kjv: The dead praise not the LORD, neither any that go down into silence.
bibleSpine.gloss: The dead go down into silence, not to conscious reward. Death is stillness of the whole being, not the liberation of a soul.

bibleSpine.kjv: Behold, all souls are mine; as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is mine: the soul that sinneth, it shall die.
bibleSpine.gloss: The soul is mortal and can die — Scripture's flat denial that the soul is immortal. Since man IS a soul, the soul that sins is the whole man, and it dies.

bibleSpine.kjv: Who only hath immortality, dwelling in the light which no man can approach unto; whom no man hath seen, nor can see: to whom be honour and power everlasting. Amen.
bibleSpine.gloss: God ONLY hath immortality. If God alone is inherently immortal, man is not — man is mortal by nature and can receive immortality only as a gift.

bibleSpine.kjv: And so it is written, The first man Adam was made a living soul; the last Adam was made a quickening spirit.
bibleSpine.gloss: Paul confirms Genesis 2:7's wording: Adam WAS MADE a living soul — a created, dependent being — set over against the last Adam who is life-giving.

bibleSpine.kjv: For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive.
bibleSpine.gloss: All die in Adam (the mortal first man); life comes only in Christ. Immortality is not innate but is 'made alive' in Christ at the resurrection.

bibleSpine.kjv: For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality.
bibleSpine.gloss: Man is 'this mortal' now; immortality is something to be PUT ON at the resurrection, not a possession he already carries. Seals the mortality of the present man.

bibleSpine.kjv: But is now made manifest by the appearing of our Saviour Jesus Christ, who hath abolished death, and hath brought life and immortality to light through the gospel:
bibleSpine.gloss: Life and immortality come to light through Christ and the gospel — proof they are a gift brought by the Saviour, not native to fallen man.

symbolDefs.symbol: the living soul (= the whole man)
symbolDefs.meaning: The living soul is not a part inside man but the WHOLE man himself — the sum produced when God joined dust (body) to the breath of life. Scripture's own equation is dust + breath = a living soul (Gen. 2:7); Paul restates it, 'the first man Adam WAS MADE a living soul' (1 Cor. 15:45). Man does not HAVE a soul; he IS one, an indivisible unit. Therefore the soul is mortal — 'the soul that sinneth, it shall die' (Ezek. 18:4) — and at death the man simply ceases to be conscious (Eccl. 9:5; Ps. 146:4). Sin and salvation happen in this one undivided being, not in an immortal ghost lodged within him.

symbolDefs.symbol: the breath / spirit of life (= God's life-power, not a conscious entity)
symbolDefs.meaning: The breath (Heb. neshamah) and spirit (Heb. ruach) of life is the impersonal, God-given life-power that animates the dust — not a self-aware being. 'The Spirit of God hath made me, and the breath of the Almighty hath given me life' (Job 33:4); Job calls it 'the spirit of God in my nostrils' (Job 27:3). The same breath of life is in beasts (Gen. 7:22), and when God 'takest away their breath, they die' (Ps. 104:29). At death it 'returns unto God who gave it' (Eccl. 12:7) as life-power reverting to its Source — and in that same instant 'his thoughts perish' (Ps. 146:4), proving the returning spirit carries no consciousness. It is God's loaned inspiration, sustained heartbeat by heartbeat (Job 34:14-15), never a detachable immortal self.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: When God had made man in His image, the human form was perfect in all its arrangements, but it was without life. Then a personal, self-existing God breathed into that form the breath of life, and man became a living, breathing, intelligent being.... Man became a living soul.
witnesses.gloss: Confirms Genesis 2:7 exactly: the formed body was lifeless until God breathed in the breath of life, and the WHOLE man 'became a living soul' — the soul is the sum, not an added occupant.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: Then a personal, self-existing God breathed into that form the breath of life, and man became a living, breathing, intelligent being.... Man became a living soul. Through Jesus Christ a personal God created man and endowed him with intelligence and power.
witnesses.gloss: Parallel confirmation that dust + the breath of life = a living soul; intelligence itself is God's endowment upon the formed man, not the property of a pre-existing immortal spirit.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: The heart beats, pulse succeeds pulse, breath succeeds breath, but the entire being is under the supervision of God.... Each heartbeat, each breath, is the inspiration of Him who breathed into the nostrils of Adam the breath of life—the inspiration of the ever-present God, the great I AM.
witnesses.gloss: Confirms the breath is God's continually-sustained life-power (the same act as Gen. 2:7), not a self-running conscious entity — man lives only by borrowed, moment-by-moment inspiration from God.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: Immortality, promised to man on condition of obedience, had been forfeited by transgression. Adam could not transmit to his posterity that which he did not possess... And only through Christ can immortality be obtained.
witnesses.gloss: Confirms 1 Tim. 6:16 and 1 Cor. 15:53: man is mortal by nature; immortality was forfeited and is obtainable only as a gift through Christ, never innate in the fallen soul.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: The great original lie which he told to Eve in Eden, 'Ye shall not surely die,' was the first sermon ever preached on the immortality of the soul. That sermon was crowned with success, and terrible results followed.
witnesses.gloss: Confirms Genesis 3:4: the immortal-soul doctrine is the serpent's original lie against man's God-declared mortality — naming the counter-doctrine this section refutes.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: Nowhere in the Sacred Scriptures is found the statement that the righteous go to their reward or the wicked to their punishment at death.... The Bible clearly teaches that the dead do not go immediately to heaven. They are represented as sleeping until the resurrection.... In the very day when the silver cord is loosed and the golden bowl broken (Ecclesiastes 12:6), man's thoughts perish.
witnesses.gloss: Confirms Eccl. 9:5, Ps. 146:4 and Job 14:10-12: the dead sleep unconsciously until the resurrection; thoughts perish at death — no soul is awake in the intermediate state.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: The theory of the immortality of the soul was one of those false doctrines that Rome, borrowing from paganism, incorporated into the religion of Christendom. Martin Luther classed it with the 'monstrous fables that form part of the Roman dunghill of decretals.'
witnesses.gloss: Confirms the historical origin of the counter-doctrine: the immortal soul is a pagan import, not a Bible teaching — establishing that Scripture's whole-man mortality is the original truth.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: One day I listened to a conversation... to the effect that the soul had not natural immortality. Some of the minister's proof texts were repeated. Among them I remember these impressed me very forcibly: 'The soul that sinneth, it shall die.' Ezekiel 18:4. 'The living know that they shall die: but the dead know not anything.' Ecclesiastes 9:5. '...who only hath immortality.' 1 Timothy 6:15, 16.
witnesses.gloss: Confirms the exact spine of this section — Ezek. 18:4, Eccl. 9:5, and 1 Tim. 6:16 cited together as proof that the soul has no natural immortality.

witnesses.author: Source Book for Bible Students (quoting Rev. William Hales, D.D.)
witnesses.quote: Nature of Man, Dr. Hales on Immortality Only in Christ.—But when it is said that man was made 'an heir' of immortality... this is not to be understood as being derived from any inherent virtue in his nature; as if the spirit or mind was necessarily immortal.... The divine sentence pronounced on Adam, 'Dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return' (Genesis 3:19), included the dissolution of the spirit also.
witnesses.gloss: Pioneer-corpus witness confirming Gen. 3:19, 1 Cor. 15:53 and 1 Tim. 6:16: immortality is not inherent in man's nature or spirit; 'dust thou art' dissolves the whole man, spirit included — immortality comes only in Christ at the resurrection.

historyAnchor: The immortal-soul doctrine entered Christendom from pagan (Greek/Platonic) philosophy through Rome, and the Reformer Martin Luther rejected it as a Romish fable (DD 17.1).
uncertainties: Several richly on-point periodical and manuscript sources surfaced in search (e.g., 14LtMs Ms 16 1899 par. 4 and 18LtMs Ms 102 1903 par. 38, both quoting Gen. 2:7 in full, and HR May 1 1873 par. 2) but their refcodes contain commas that crash the local exact-lookup FTS parser, so I could not re-verify the paragraph text on demand; I therefore cited only clean book-form refcodes (CCh, 8T, MH, 1SM, GC, DD, CET, 1T, SBBS) that resolve reliably. MH 415.1 is an exact parallel to CCh 74.4/8T 264.1 and is available as a substitute if a redundant citation is trimmed.

The transcript leans on Strong's/Hebrew word meanings (neshamah, ruach) to argue breath = mind/intellect; I grounded the symbols in Scripture's usage rather than lexical gloss, since the section's doctrine (breath = impersonal life-power, not a conscious mind) rests more safely on Ps. 146:4 / Job 34:14-15 / Eccl. 12:7 than on asserting the breath is itself 'the mind.'
